statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-84008 (GHSA-846f-f764-76mx, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-846f-f764-76mx): SignedCms.CheckSignature can repeatedly reparse attacker-controlled X.509 data, causing unauthenticated quadratic CPU exhaustion. Affected: System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 10.0.0 to 10.0.12, fixed in 10.0.13; Microsoft shipped the fix in .NET 10.0.13 (SDK 10.0.113 and 10.0.402): https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/468, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md. The dotnet10-sdk package ships its own copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs.dll under /usr/lib/dotnet/sdk/<version>/ (the SDK root and FSharp directories, plus a Windows-specific runtimes/win copy), which the dotnet CLI, MSBuild, NuGet and F# tools load. Scanned every package built from the dotnet10-sdk source for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI Alpine repository (10.0.204-r0 to 10.0.303-r3, 8 builds; x86_64 and aarch64; including the -dbg, templates and doc subpackages, recursing into zip and NuGet archives) and read the version resources of every copy and the package versions recorded in the SDK's .deps.json files; both architectures match in every build. 10.0.204-r0, 10.0.301-r0, 10.0.302-r0, 10.0.302-r1 and 10.0.303-r0 carry System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 10.0.8 to 10.0.12 (assembly product versions 10.0.8 to 10.0.12), inside the affected range; 10.0.303-r1 and every later build carry 10.0.13 to 10.0.15 (the assemblies in 10.0.303-r1 report product version 10.0.13 although the SDK version is still 10.0.303), which include the fix; the 10.0.13 assembly is also larger than the 10.0.12 one.

CVE-2026-84008 (GHSA-846f-f764-76mx, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-846f-f764-76mx): SignedCms.CheckSignature can repeatedly reparse attacker-controlled X.509 data, causing unauthenticated quadratic CPU exhaustion. Affected: System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 8.0.0 to 8.0.1, fixed in 8.0.2; Microsoft shipped the fix in .NET 8.0.32 (SDK 8.0.132 and 8.0.426): https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/468, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md. The dotnet8-sdk package ships its own copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs.dll under /usr/lib/dotnet/sdk/<version>/ (the SDK root, FSharp and Containers/tasks directories, plus a Windows-specific runtimes/win copy), which the dotnet CLI, MSBuild, NuGet and F# tools load. Scanned every package built from the dotnet8-sdk source for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository (8.0.123-r0 to 8.0.134-r0, 9 builds, as 8.0.128, 8.0.130 and 8.0.132 were not published for 3.23; x86_64 and aarch64; including the -dbg, templates and doc subpackages, recursing into zip and NuGet archives) and read the version resources of every copy and the package versions recorded in the SDK's .deps.json files; both architectures match in every build. 8.0.123-r0 to 8.0.131-r0 carry System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 8.0.1 (built from .NET runtime 8.0.23 to 8.0.31 sources), inside the affected range; 8.0.133-r0 and every later build carry System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 8.0.2 (built from .NET runtime 8.0.33 and later sources), which includes the fix; the fixed assembly is also larger than the previous one. The Roslyn build-task .deps.json still records an older 6.0 reference to the package, but no 6.0 copy of the assembly ships in any build.

CVE-2026-84008 (GHSA-846f-f764-76mx): SignedCms.CheckSignature in System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs can repeatedly reparse attacker-controlled X.509 data, causing quadratic CPU use. Microsoft fixed it in System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 10.0.13, shipped with .NET 10.0.13; versions 10.0.0 to 10.0.12 are affected (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-846f-f764-76mx, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/468). DHI dotnet-sdk-10 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET SDK. Unpacked every published dotnet-sdk-10 package in the DHI Debian repository, 10 builds from 10.0.301-0 to the current 10.0.404-1 for amd64 and arm64, including the .nupkg archives inside them, and read the file and product version of every copy of System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs.dll; both architectures agree in every build. Each build carries copies in the ASP.NET Core shared framework (shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App) and in the SDK directory and its FSharp directory, each also under runtimes/win/lib/net10.0 in the SDK and FSharp directories, and in each build every copy has the same version: 10.0.9 in 10.0.301-0, 10.0.10 in 10.0.302-0 and 10.0.302-1, 10.0.11 in 10.0.400-1, 10.0.12 in 10.0.401-0 and 10.0.401-1, 10.0.13 in 10.0.402-0, 10.0.14 in 10.0.403-0, and 10.0.15 in 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1. No .nupkg archive in these packages contains it. The dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages from the same source hold only a configuration file and a changelog. So 10.0.402-0 is the first build with the fixed assembly, and every earlier build carries an affected version. The range ends at 10.0.402-0.
